2608.00747.title: When Prompts Control Robots: Prompt Injection Attacks in Multi-Agent Robotic Systems
2608.00747.paper_summary: Large language models are increasingly integrated into autonomous robotic systems for task planning and control, but this integration exposes them to prompt injection attacks that can lead to unsafe decisions and physical harm. Multi-agent settings increase the risks through cross-agent contamination and broader attack surfaces. In this paper, we evaluate prompt injection attacks against an LLM-based multi-agent robotic system, considering both direct injections into task instructions and indirect injections through perception modules. In our experiments across varying attack-goal complexities and injection strategies in both single-agent and multi-agent settings, we show that prompt injection can induce adversarial actions while reducing task completion. We find that attacks can propagate from one agent to others through shared prompt structures, with impacts varying depending on prompt composition and the targeted agent. We further analyze how architectural changes affect LLM queries and, consequently, the attack success. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study that systematically investigates prompt injection attacks in a multi-agent LLM-based robotic system.
2608.00747.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型越來越多地被整合進自主機器人系統中，以進行任務規劃和控制，但這種整合使它們暴露於提示注入攻擊之下，可能導致不安全的決策和身體傷害。多代理環境通過跨代理污染和更廣泛的攻擊面增加了風險。在本文中，我們評估了針對基於LLM的多代理機器人系統的提示注入攻擊，考慮了直接注入任務指令和通過感知模塊的間接注入。在我們的實驗中，涵蓋了不同攻擊目標的複雜性和注入策略，無論是在單代理還是多代理環境中，我們顯示提示注入可以誘導對抗性行為，同時降低任務完成率。我們發現攻擊可以通過共享的提示結構從一個代理傳播到其他代理，影響因提示組成和目標代理而異。我們進一步分析了架構變化如何影響LLM查詢，從而影響攻擊的成功率。據我們所知，這是第一項系統性研究基於LLM的多代理機器人系統中的提示注入攻擊的研究。
